item.title: Hisense HMC6MBK 7-in-1 Pressure Cooker 1000W

item.title: Abasi 5% EC Insecticide (1 Litre) 1 Litre
item.description: Abasi 5% EC (1 litre) Spider mites, thrips and leafminers are small, but they reduce yield and spoil the look of roses, tomatoes, cucumbers and French beans, which is what buyers pay for. Abasi 5% EC is an abamectin insecticide that kills by contact and stomach action and moves through the leaf (translaminar), so pests feeding on the underside are reached. It works at very low rates. KEY BENEFITS • Strong knockdown of mites and leaf-mining insects • Contact and stomach activity stops pests feeding quickly • Translaminar movement protects both leaf surfaces • Reliable on thrips and other small sucking pests • Cost-efficient: only 4 to 6 ml per 20 L knapsack TECHNICAL SPECS • Active ingredient: Abamectin 5% (50 g/L) • Formulation: Emulsifiable concentrate (EC) • IRAC group 6: activates glutamate-gated chloride channels, causing paralysis • Pack: 1 litre (also available in 50 ml, 100 ml, 250 ml, 500 ml and 1 L) • Crops and pests: thrips, spider mites and nematode dips on roses; spider mites and caterpillars on tomatoes; leafminers and aphids on cucumbers; leafminers, thrips, spider mites and aphids on French beans MIXING AND APPLICATION DOSAGE (per 20 L knapsack) Rate: 200 to 300 ml per hectare in 1,000 L of water, which is 4 to 6 ml per 20 L knapsack. A 1-litre bottle mixes about 166 to 250 knapsacks. 1. Half-fill the knapsack with clean water. 2. Add the measured Abasi, then top up to 20 L and agitate well. 3. Spray immediately after mixing, covering the undersides of leaves where mites and thrips hide. 4. Follow the repeat interval and harvest waiting period printed on your pack. SAFETY Toxic to bees and aquatic life, so avoid spraying during flowering or near water. Wear gloves, mask and overalls. Do not eat, drink or smoke while spraying. WHAT'S IN THE BOX 1 × Abasi 5% EC (1 litre) ORDER Pay by M-Pesa. Delivery to all 47 counties, or pick up at The Sarit Centre, Westlands, Nairobi.

item.title: Promax 20 EC Odourless Bed Bug Insecticide
item.description: Promax 20 EC Odourless Bed Bug Insecticide (50 ml sachet) Bed bugs, called kunguni in Swahili, hide in mattress seams, bed frames and skirting boards and bite while you sleep. Promax 20 EC is a propoxur-based, odourless insecticide concentrate that you dilute and spray straight into those hiding places. It also deals with cockroaches (mende), fleas, ants and houseflies, so one sachet protects a house, hostel room, hotel room or office. KEY FEATURES • Odourless formulation suited to bedrooms and other indoor spaces • Residual action on treated surfaces, so pests that crawl across later are still affected • Multi-pest: bed bugs, cockroaches, fleas, ants and houseflies • Concentrated: 25 ml makes 1 litre of ready-to-spray liquid • Works with any hand-pump or knapsack sprayer SPECIFICATIONS • Active ingredient: Propoxur 20% w/v (carbamate insecticide) • Formulation: Emulsifiable concentrate (EC) • Use: household and public-health crawling-insect control • Pack: 50 ml sachet, which makes 2 litres of spray • Mode of action: blocks nerve signal transmission, causing paralysis WHERE IT HELPS Bed bugs bite at night and hide by day in mattress seams, bed frames, headboards, skirting boards and cracks. Cockroaches, fleas, ants and houseflies use the same cracks and corners to travel and breed. Promax stays active on treated surfaces, so pests that crawl across them later are still affected, which helps in bedrooms, hostel rooms and offices where you cannot spray every day. MIXING RATES (FROM THE PRODUCT LABEL) • 1 litre hand sprayer: 25 ml Promax 20 EC, topped up with water to 1 litre • 5 litre garden sprayer: 125 ml, topped up to 5 litres • 20 litre knapsack: 500 ml, topped up to 20 litres • Most homes need only 1 to 5 litres; the knapsack rate is for hotels, hostels and large premises • Always confirm the rate on your pack's label before mixing HOW TO USE IT Half-fill the sprayer with clean water, add Promax, top up with water and shake well. Spray mattress seams, bed frames, headboards, skirting boards, cracks, the backs of sockets and furniture joints. Wet the surfaces lightly and do not soak them. Bed bug eggs can hatch later, so inspect after about two weeks and treat again if needed. BEFORE YOU START • Strip the bed and wash bedding at a high temperature • Vacuum the mattress, frame and floor • Do not spray food, utensils or bedding you will use before it dries SAFETY Keep children, pets and fish tanks out of the room until surfaces are dry and the room is ventilated. Wear gloves and wash your hands after use. Odourless does not mean harmless: it is still an insecticide, so keep it away from food, water and children. STORAGE Keep the sachet or any leftover concentrate sealed in its original pack, in a cool, dry, locked place. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS How much spray does one 50 ml sachet make? One 50 ml sachet makes 2 litres of ready-to-spray liquid, at 25 ml per litre. Always confirm the rate on the label of your pack before mixing. Will I smell it after spraying? The formulation is odourless, so it suits bedrooms. Let surfaces dry fully, ventilate the room and keep people and pets out until then. Does one treatment remove bed bugs? Eggs can hatch later, so inspect after about two weeks and treat again if you still see bugs. item.title: Premise 200 SC Termiticide 50 ml
item.description: Premise 200 SC Termiticide (50 ml, 1 litre) Termites (mchwa) rarely announce themselves. They eat door frames, roof timbers and cupboards from the inside until the damage is expensive. Bayer Premise 200 SC is a non-repellent, odourless termiticide with imidacloprid 200 g/L. Termites walk through the treated soil without detecting it, carry the active ingredient back and spread it through the colony. KEY FEATURES • Non-repellent with a transfer effect, so it reaches termites you cannot see • Suitable for pre-construction and post-construction treatment • Also listed for controlling ants • Practically odourless at the recommended dilution • Delivered to all 47 counties SPECIFICATIONS • Brand: Premise, made by Bayer • Active ingredient: Imidacloprid 200 g/L (neonicotinoid) • Formulation: Suspension concentrate (SC) • Applications: foundations, slab preparation, trenches, termite mounds and wall voids • Pack sizes: 50 ml and 1 litre WHERE IT HELPS It suits a builder treating hardcore and soil before the slab is cast, a homeowner treating the foundation lines of an existing house, and anyone dealing with a termite mound or wall void. MIXING RATES (FROM THE PRODUCT LABEL) • Dilution: 50 ml Premise 200 SC per 20 L knapsack of water (0.25%) • Application volume: 5 L of mixed solution per m² of soil, or per linear metre of trench along foundations • One knapsack covers about 4 m² or 4 linear metres • A 1 litre bottle mixes 20 knapsacks (400 L), enough for about 80 m² or 80 linear metres HOW TO USE IT Shake the bottle vigorously, half fill the knapsack with clean water, add the measured Premise, top up to 20 L and stir. Pre-construction: treat the hardcore and soil before the slab is cast. Trenches: apply along the inside and outside of the foundation lines. Existing buildings: drill and inject along foundations and slab joints, and for a mound, drill into the nest and drench it thoroughly. Do not apply in rain or when rain is expected, and wash all equipment after use. Check the rates against the label on your pack. BEFORE YOU START • Fix leaks and remove old stumps and buried timber near the building • Keep treated soil away from wells, boreholes and drains • For a large building, consider a licensed pest control operator SAFETY Harmful. Wear gloves, overalls, boots and a mask when mixing and spraying. It is toxic to bees and aquatic life, so never let spray or wash water reach streams, ponds, wells or drains. STORAGE Store the unused product in its original, closed pack in a cool, dry, locked place, away from food, feed and children. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS How does Premise 200 SC kill the whole colony? It is non-repellent, so termites cross the treated soil without detecting it. They carry the active ingredient back and spread it through the colony. How much does one knapsack of Premise cover? Mixed at 50 ml per 20 L and applied at 5 L per m², one knapsack treats about 4 m² of soil or 4 linear metres of trench. Confirm the rates on your label. Which pack should I choose, 50 ml or 1 litre? The 50 ml pack makes one 20 L knapsack, which suits a small job. The 1 litre bottle makes twenty, which suits a house or a building site. item.title: Syngenta Tatua Rat and Mice Poison Blocks

In a farm store or a poultry house, rodents eat and spoil feed and disturb the birds. A block is heavy and solid, so it resists damp and handling better than loose bait, and it can be fixed inside a station so that it is not scattered. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS Why are bait blocks used in stations? A block fixed inside a station is not scattered or carried off, and children, pets and livestock cannot reach it. Where should I place the stations? Along walls, near holes, behind stacked goods and in dark corners where you find droppings, gnaw marks and runways. Can I use the blocks in a poultry house? Lysine is an essential amino acid. Amino acids are the building blocks of protein, and animals cannot make lysine themselves, so it must come from the feed. In poultry and pigs, lysine is the amino acid that is most often short in cereal-based rations such as those made mostly with maize. When lysine is short, growth slows, feed conversion worsens and muscle development suffers. WHY ADD LYSINE TO RATIONS Adding lysine helps farmers and feed mixers balance rations so that animals get the amino acids they need. This can support growth, feed efficiency and meat yield in pigs and broilers, and egg production in layers. It also helps balance protein levels in feed formulations, which can help reduce the amount of protein-rich ingredients needed. WHERE IT IS USED • Poultry rations: chicks, broilers, growers and layers • Pig rations: weaners, growers and finishers The correct amount depends on the species, age, production level and the other ingredients in the ration. HOW TO USE IT Read and follow the label and inclusion rate before use. Add lysine to the ration at the rate recommended on the label or by your nutritionist or vet. A coefficient of 18 to 20 means the fluid is many times stronger than phenol when tested under standard laboratory conditions, which is why it is described as a powerful disinfectant. item.title: Jambo Clean Foliar Fertilizer
item.description: Greenlife Jambo Clean Foliar Fertilizer (1 Litre) Greenlife Jambo Clean is a foliar fertilizer that cleans sooty mould and honeydew off crops while nourishing them. It contains water-soluble phosphorus pentoxide (P2O5) 8.2% and total nitrogen 10.0% (urea 8.5% plus ammoniacal 1.5%). It is supplied in a 1 litre pack. KEY FEATURES • Foliar fertilizer that cleans sooty mould and honeydew • Water-soluble phosphorus pentoxide (P2O5) 8.2% • Total nitrogen 10.0% (urea 8.5% + ammoniacal 1.5%) • Feeds the crop while it cleans the leaves • 1 litre pack • Greenlife brand • Delivered to all 47 counties WHAT ARE HONEYDEW AND SOOTY MOULD? Sucking insects such as aphids, whiteflies and scale insects feed on plant sap and pass out a sticky, sugary liquid called honeydew. It covers leaves, stems and fruits. A black fungus called sooty mould then grows on the honeydew and forms a dark coating. The coating blocks light, so the plant cannot photosynthesise well, and it makes the crop look dirty, which can lower quality and market value, especially for flowers, vegetables and fruit. HOW JAMBO CLEAN HELPS Jambo Clean is sprayed on the crop to help clean off sooty mould and honeydew. At the same time, the nutrients in the product nourish the plant. This makes it a practical choice for growers who need to clean up their crops and give them a boost. WHAT THE NUTRIENTS DO • Nitrogen supports leaf growth and green colour. Here it comes partly as urea and partly as ammoniacal nitrogen • Phosphorus supports root development, flowering and energy transfer in the plant HOW TO USE IT Follow the dose, water volume, timing and interval given on the label. Mix in clean water, agitate, and spray evenly so that leaves are well covered. Spray in the cool of the morning or late afternoon and avoid the heat of the day to reduce the risk of leaf scorch. Test on a few plants first if you are using it on a crop for the first time. IMPORTANT: TREAT THE CAUSE TOO Sooty mould returns if the sucking insects are still there. Scout for aphids, whiteflies and scale and control them with a suitable insecticide, following its label. Good crop hygiene, ant control and removing badly affected leaves also help. SAFETY Read the label before use. Wear gloves and avoid contact with eyes and skin. Keep away from children, pets, food and water. Do not let spray or rinse water reach streams or ponds. STORAGE Store in the original closed bottle in a cool, dry place away from food and feed. item.title: BioDistinction Extra 700SC Copper Fertilizer
item.description: Greenlife BioDistinction Extra 700SC Copper Fertilizer (1 Litre) Greenlife BioDistinction Extra 700SC is a liquid chelated copper suspension concentrate fertilizer. It contains copper oxychloride 700 g/L, which is 400 g/L metallic copper equivalent, and it corrects and prevents copper deficiency in vegetables, fruit, cereals and ornamentals. It is supplied in a 1 litre pack. KEY FEATURES • Liquid chelated copper fertilizer in suspension concentrate (SC) form • Copper oxychloride 700 g/L (400 g/L metallic copper equivalent) • Corrects and prevents copper deficiency • For vegetables, fruit, cereals and ornamentals • 1 litre pack • Greenlife brand WHY COPPER MATTERS Copper is a trace element that plants need in small amounts. It plays a part in enzyme activity, in the formation of chlorophyll and in flowering, pollen formation and grain filling. When copper is short, plants can show stunted growth, pale or twisted young leaves, poor flowering and lower yields. Cereals are especially sensitive, and deficiencies are more common in sandy, peaty and very high-organic soils. HOW TO USE IT Apply as directed on the label, normally as a foliar spray, using the dose and water volume recommended for your crop. Mix by half-filling the tank with water, adding the measured product, topping up and agitating well. Spray evenly, covering the leaves. Apply when the crop is actively growing and at the stage recommended on the label, and spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when it is cooler. If you are unsure whether copper is really short, consider a soil or leaf test to confirm. GOOD PRACTICE • Do not exceed the label rate, because too much copper can harm plants and soil • Avoid spraying in hot midday sun • Test a small area first if you plan to mix with other products • Keep records of dates and doses SAFETY Read the label before use. Wear gloves, a mask, goggles and protective clothing when mixing and spraying, and wash well afterwards. Keep away from children, pets, food and water. Copper compounds can be harmful to fish and aquatic life, so keep spray and rinse water out of streams, ponds and drains. STORAGE Store in the original closed bottle in a cool, dry place away from food and feed. Shake well before use. ORDER Order BioDistinction Extra 700SC online, pay by M-Pesa and get delivery to all 47 counties, or pick up at The Sarit Centre, Westlands, Nairobi.

item.description: Albafas 10% Albendazole Drench (500 ml) Albafas is a 10% w/v albendazole drench for treating worms and liver fluke in cattle, sheep, goats and camels. It is supplied in a 500 ml bottle from Norbrook Kenya, and it is used against roundworms, lungworms, tapeworms and liver fluke. KEY FEATURES • 10% w/v albendazole, a broad-spectrum dewormer • For cattle, sheep, goats and camels • Used against roundworms, lungworms, tapeworms and liver fluke • 500 ml bottle • Made by Norbrook Kenya WHY WORM CONTROL MATTERS Internal parasites quietly drain animals. Heavily infected cattle, sheep, goats and camels grow slowly, lose condition, produce less milk and meat, and become more open to other diseases. Young animals are often the most affected. Regular, well-planned deworming protects growth and productivity and can save the cost of treating sick animals later. HOW TO USE IT Albafas is given by mouth as a drench. The dose depends on the animal species and body weight, so follow the dose on the label and use an accurate drenching gun. Weigh or estimate weight carefully, and dose the heaviest animal in a group at its own weight to avoid under-dosing. Under-dosing is one of the main causes of worms becoming resistant to dewormers. If you are not sure about the dose, the correct time to treat, or the withdrawal period for milk and meat, ask your vet or animal health provider. GOOD PRACTICE • Deworm on a programme agreed with your vet, rather than only when animals look sick • Keep clean water and good pasture management to reduce re-infection • Rotate dewormers from different groups when advised, to help slow resistance • Keep records of dates, products and doses SAFETY AND STORAGE For veterinary use. Follow the label dose and withdrawal periods. Wear gloves when handling and wash your hands afterwards. Keep out of reach of children. Store the bottle tightly closed in a cool, dry place away from direct sun and food. Do not let rinse water reach streams or ponds. item.title: Amaze Fridge and Freezer Guard with 6-Way Extension Socket
item.description: Buy the Amaze Fridge and Freezer Guard with a 6-way extension socket online in Kenya. Power cuts, sudden returns of electricity and low voltage are some of the most common reasons fridge compressors fail. This guard sits between your wall socket and your fridge or freezer, watches the supply, and cuts the power when it is unsafe so your appliance is not damaged. How it works: the guard has three indicator lights marked OFF, WAIT and ON. When the supply is unsafe it disconnects the appliance. When power returns, the guard waits for a short delay before switching back on, which gives the compressor time to settle. This protects against the damaging quick restart that often happens when electricity comes back after an outage. A bypass button lets you override the guard if you need to. The bundle also includes an Amaze 6-way extension socket with a long white cable and a UK-style plug, so you can power your TV, decoder, phone chargers and other small devices from a single wall point. Pack size: 1 Amaze fridge and freezer guard plus 1 Amaze 6-way extension socket with cable. Colour: white with blue label. Plug type: UK three-pin. Please check the rating printed on the guard against your appliance before you buy, and use the guard for refrigeration appliances as shown on its label. item.description: Bat CRP Bat Repellent (250 ml, 500 ml and 1 litre) Bats that settle in a roof or ceiling leave droppings and urine that stain ceilings, cause strong smells and attract insects, and their noise at night disturbs families, guests and worshippers. Heavily infected cattle, sheep, goats and camels grow slowly, lose condition, produce less milk and meat, and become more open to other diseases. Young animals are often the most affected. Regular, well-planned deworming protects growth and productivity and can save the cost of treating sick animals later. HOW TO USE IT Albafas is given by mouth as a drench. If you are not sure about the dose, the correct time to treat, or the withdrawal period for milk and meat, ask your vet or animal health provider. GOOD PRACTICE • Deworm on a programme agreed with your vet, rather than only when animals look sick • Keep clean water and good pasture management to reduce re-infection • Rotate dewormers from different groups when advised, to help slow resistance • Keep records of dates, products and doses SAFETY AND STORAGE For veterinary use. item.title: Albafas 10% Albendazole Drench 1 Litre
item.description: Albafas 10% Albendazole Drench (1 Litre) Albafas is a 10% w/v albendazole drench for treating worms and liver fluke in cattle, sheep, goats and camels. It is supplied in a 500 ml bottle from Norbrook Kenya, and it is used against roundworms, lungworms, tapeworms and liver fluke. KEY FEATURES • 10% w/v albendazole, a broad-spectrum dewormer • For cattle, sheep, goats and camels • Used against roundworms, lungworms, tapeworms and liver fluke • 500 ml bottle • Made by Norbrook Kenya WHY WORM CONTROL MATTERS Internal parasites quietly drain animals. Heavily infected cattle, sheep, goats and camels grow slowly, lose condition, produce less milk and meat, and become more open to other diseases. Young animals are often the most affected. Regular, well-planned deworming protects growth and productivity and can save the cost of treating sick animals later. HOW TO USE IT Albafas is given by mouth as a drench. The dose depends on the animal species and body weight, so follow the dose on the label and use an accurate drenching gun. Weigh or estimate weight carefully, and dose the heaviest animal in a group at its own weight to avoid under-dosing. Under-dosing is one of the main causes of worms becoming resistant to dewormers. If you are not sure about the dose, the correct time to treat, or the withdrawal period for milk and meat, ask your vet or animal health provider. GOOD PRACTICE • Deworm on a programme agreed with your vet, rather than only when animals look sick • Keep clean water and good pasture management to reduce re-infection • Rotate dewormers from different groups when advised, to help slow resistance • Keep records of dates, products and doses SAFETY AND STORAGE For veterinary use. Follow the label dose and withdrawal periods. Wear gloves when handling and wash your hands afterwards. Keep out of reach of children. Store the bottle tightly closed in a cool, dry place away from direct sun and food. Do not let rinse water reach streams or ponds. item.title: Actellic 50EC Insecticide 500 ml
item.description: Actellic 50EC Insecticide (100 ml, 250 ml, 500 ml, 1 litre) Weevils and moths can turn a full store of maize into dust within months. Actellic 50EC is an organophosphate emulsifiable concentrate with pirimiphos-methyl 500 g/L. It acts by contact, ingestion and fumigant action, and it keeps working on walls, floors and bag surfaces after you spray. KEY FEATURES • Controls weevils, beetles, moths, flies and wasps • Acts by contact, ingestion and fumigant action • Keeps working on treated walls, floors and bag surfaces • Three uses: store surface spray, bagged grain and grain admixture SPECIFICATIONS • Brand: Actellic • Product: 50EC insecticide • Active ingredient: Pirimiphos-methyl 500 g/L (49.02% w/w) • Formulation: Emulsifiable concentrate (EC) • Chemical group: Organophosphate • Pack sizes: 100 ml, 250 ml, 500 ml, 1 litre WHERE IT HELPS Insects arrive with the harvest and hide in cracks, on walls and on bag surfaces, so the building needs treating as well as the grain. Actellic 50EC covers three jobs: surface spraying of stores and livestock houses, treating bagged grain, and mixing into stored grain as an admixture. MIXING RATES (FROM THE PRODUCT LABEL) • Walls, floors, empty stores and livestock houses: 100 ml in 10 L of water (200 ml per 20 L knapsack) • Bagged grain and bag stacks: 50 to 100 ml in 5 L of water per 100 m² (200 to 400 ml per 20 L knapsack). Use the higher end for an existing infestation • Admixture to stored grain: 8 ml per tonne of grain, diluted in 0.75 to 1.5 L of water (not mixed in the knapsack) • Coverage: about 5 L of spray per 100 m². Porous surfaces such as concrete, brick and unpainted wood may need up to 15 L per 100 m² • One 20 L tank covers roughly 400 m² on normal surfaces and about 130 m² on porous ones HOW TO USE IT Clean and sweep the store first, removing old grain and debris, then spray to wet all surfaces without run-off. For admixture, dilute the measured amount in the water volume shown and apply it to the grain, not in the knapsack. These are the rates the catalog already published for this product, so check them against the label on your pack before mixing. Do not use Actellic 50EC with thermal foggers. BEFORE YOU START • Remove food, feed and animals before spraying • Ventilate the store afterwards • Measure the area first, so that you mix only the volume you need SAFETY Actellic 50EC is an organophosphate, so wear gloves, a mask and overalls when mixing and spraying, and keep children, pets, food, feed and water away. Label grain treated by admixture as chemically treated, and follow any waiting period on the pack. STORAGE Store the bottle closed, in its original container, in a cool, dry, locked place away from food and feed. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS Which pests does Actellic 50EC control? The catalog lists weevils, beetles, moths, flies and wasps. Can I use Actellic 50EC in a thermal fogger? No. The catalog advice for this product is not to use it with thermal foggers. How much does one 20 L knapsack cover? About 400 m² on normal surfaces and roughly 130 m² on porous ones such as concrete, brick and unpainted wood. item.title: Abasi 5% EC 100 ml
item.description: Abasi 5% EC (100 ml) Spider mites, thrips and leafminers are small, but they reduce yield and spoil the look of roses, tomatoes, cucumbers and French beans, which is what buyers pay for. Abasi 5% EC is an abamectin insecticide that kills by contact and stomach action and moves through the leaf (translaminar), so pests feeding on the underside are reached. It works at very low rates. KEY BENEFITS • Strong knockdown of mites and leaf-mining insects • Contact and stomach activity stops pests feeding quickly • Translaminar movement protects both leaf surfaces • Reliable on thrips and other small sucking pests • Cost-efficient: only 4 to 6 ml per 20 L knapsack TECHNICAL SPECS • Active ingredient: Abamectin 5% (50 g/L) • Formulation: Emulsifiable concentrate (EC) • IRAC group 6: activates glutamate-gated chloride channels, causing paralysis • Pack: 100 ml (also available in 50 ml, 100 ml, 250 ml, 500 ml and 1 L) • Crops and pests: thrips, spider mites and nematode dips on roses; spider mites and caterpillars on tomatoes; leafminers and aphids on cucumbers; leafminers, thrips, spider mites and aphids on French beans MIXING AND APPLICATION DOSAGE (per 20 L knapsack) Rate: 200 to 300 ml per hectare in 1,000 L of water, which is 4 to 6 ml per 20 L knapsack. A 100 ml pack mixes about 16 to 25 knapsacks. 1. Half-fill the knapsack with clean water. 2. Add the measured Abasi, then top up to 20 L and agitate well. 3. Spray immediately after mixing, covering the undersides of leaves where mites and thrips hide. 4. Follow the repeat interval and harvest waiting period printed on your pack. SAFETY Toxic to bees and aquatic life, so avoid spraying during flowering or near water. Wear gloves, mask and overalls. Do not eat, drink or smoke while spraying. WHAT'S IN THE BOX 1 × Abasi 5% EC (100 ml) ORDER Pay by M-Pesa. Delivery to all 47 counties, or pick up at The Sarit Centre, Westlands, Nairobi.

Thermal receipt printing uses heat-sensitive paper, so the printer can produce text without a conventional ink cartridge or toner. This makes it a practical option for shops and service businesses that print customer receipts throughout the working day. A PRACTICAL PRINTER FOR BUSY COUNTERS A receipt printer is an important part of a point-of-sale workflow. After a sale is recorded in compatible POS software, the system can send the transaction details to the printer so the customer receives a printed record. Depending on the software and configuration, receipts may show items purchased, quantities, prices, totals, taxes, payment details and the business information configured in the POS system. The exact receipt layout is controlled by the software, not by the printer alone. The 80mm paper format provides a wider receipt area than smaller receipt formats. HOW THERMAL RECEIPT PRINTING WORKS Direct thermal printers create an image by applying heat to specially coated thermal paper. Because the printing process does not use ink cartridges, businesses do not need to purchase ink or toner for ordinary receipt printing. The paper itself is the consumable. Store thermal rolls in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight, excess heat and friction, which can affect print quality or cause receipts to darken. For consistent results, load the roll in the direction indicated by the printer's paper guide, keep the paper path clear and use rolls that meet the printer's stated width and diameter limits. If a receipt prints blank, check that the thermal paper is loaded with its coated side facing the print head. Follow the manufacturer's instructions when opening the cover or clearing a paper jam. It is designed to provide a removable outer layer that helps protect ordinary clothing from incidental dirt and limited splashes during suitable low-risk tasks. The listing identifies a white coat with a front closure and pockets. It is not described as a chemical-resistant suit, flame-resistant garment or certified barrier gown, so it should be selected only for tasks where general laboratory clothing is appropriate. WHY LAB COATS ARE WORN A laboratory coat can help prevent small amounts of dust, dirt or incidental contamination from reaching personal clothing. It can also reduce the transfer of material outside a controlled work area when it is removed before leaving the laboratory. The coat is one layer in a broader safety system; it does not replace fume hoods, glove boxes, safe handling practices, eye protection or task-specific PPE. The correct garment depends on the substances handled, the quantities involved and the possibility of splashes, heat or ignition. FIT AND COVERAGE Choose a coat that fits comfortably over the clothing worn in the laboratory. Check the chest, sleeve and overall length to ensure that the garment covers the required areas without restricting movement. Sleeves should extend to the wrists and overlap gloves where the task requires it. The front closure should fasten fully without gaping. A coat that is too loose may catch on equipment, while one that is too tight may restrict movement or expose clothing during work. Confirm available sizes and the supplier's measurement chart before ordering. MATERIAL AND HAZARD LIMITATIONS The exact fabric composition for this listing is not specified. Traditional laboratory coats may be made from cotton or polyester-cotton blends, but material choice matters. Some synthetic blends can melt or burn when exposed to flame, and ordinary coats may not provide adequate protection against significant chemical splashes, corrosives or biological hazards. Do not assume that a white coat is flame-resistant, chemical-resistant or sterile. Review the supplier's material information and choose specialist garments where the risk assessment requires them. USING A LAB COAT RESPONSIBLY Wear the coat only in the work areas for which it is intended. Keep it fastened during tasks and avoid carrying contaminated items in the pockets. Do not wear a potentially contaminated coat into eating areas, public spaces or home environments. Remove it using the workplace's hygiene procedure and wash hands after handling. If a spill or contamination occurs, follow the laboratory's incident procedure and the chemical safety data sheet rather than simply brushing off the garment. CARE AND LAUNDERING Follow the garment care label for washing, drying and ironing. Facilities may require lab coats to be laundered separately from personal clothing or by an approved laundry provider. Inspect the coat regularly for tears, loose buttons, damaged seams and worn cuffs. Replace a coat that no longer provides adequate coverage or has been contaminated beyond the approved cleaning process. Do not take a contaminated coat home unless the workplace procedure specifically permits it. CHOOSING THE RIGHT PPE FOR THE TASK For significant chemical handling, infectious materials, flammable substances or other higher-risk tasks, a standard lab coat may be insufficient. Depending on the hazard, additional gloves, eye protection, chemical apron, protective coverall or flame-resistant garment may be required. Follow the laboratory risk assessment and relevant safety guidance. The coat is a general protective clothing layer, not a substitute for engineering controls or training. item.title: Clear Anti-Fog Safety Goggles
item.description: CLEAR ANTI-FOG SAFETY GOGGLES IN KENYA Clear Anti-Fog Safety Goggles are protective eyewear intended to help shield the eyes during suitable workshop, laboratory, cleaning and maintenance tasks. Anti-fog treatment is intended to reduce misting that can interfere with visibility, but the exact lens material, ventilation design, impact rating and splash-protection standard must be confirmed from the supplier before use in a safety-critical task. WHY ENCLOSED GOGGLES MAY BE NEEDED Safety goggles provide a closer enclosure around the eye area than ordinary spectacles. Depending on their design, they may help protect against dust, flying particles or liquid splashes. The level of protection varies by model. Some goggles have direct ventilation for impact protection, while indirect or non-vented designs may be selected for dust and splash hazards. Anti-fog coating can help maintain clearer vision in humid or changing-temperature conditions, but it does not replace correct ventilation, cleaning or fit. FIT AND COMFORT The adjustable elastic strap is intended to help hold the goggles in position. Adjust the strap so the frame sits comfortably and consistently against the face without excessive pressure. Check that the goggles do not leave large gaps around the eyes and that the wearer can see clearly in all directions required for the task. If the wearer uses prescription glasses, confirm whether the goggles are designed to fit over them. Do not use eyewear that slips, distorts vision or cannot be secured properly. CHECK THE PROTECTION STANDARD Before using goggles for industrial or chemical tasks, check the markings and manufacturer documentation for the applicable eye-protection standard and hazard rating. A clear lens does not automatically mean the goggles are impact-rated, splash-rated or suitable for chemical handling. EN 166 and ANSI/ISEA Z87.1 are examples of standards used for protective eyewear, but this listing does not confirm that the product meets either standard. Do not claim a certification unless it appears on the product and supporting documentation. TASK-SPECIFIC USE These goggles may be suitable for general eye protection when the verified specification matches the hazard. For dust or flying particles, confirm the impact rating and ventilation type. For liquid splashes, check that the design provides the required splash protection and that the seal is appropriate. For chemical spraying or fumigation, follow the chemical label and risk assessment, and confirm compatibility with the other PPE being worn. Goggles alone do not protect the face, skin or respiratory system. CARE AND INSPECTION Inspect the lens and frame before each use. Do not use goggles with cracks, deep scratches, damaged straps, loose fittings or a coating that has deteriorated. Clean them using the manufacturer's recommended method and a suitable lens cloth. Avoid harsh solvents or abrasive materials that could damage the anti-fog coating. Allow the goggles to dry fully before storage and keep them in a clean protective case or pouch where possible. Replace them when visibility or fit is compromised. WORKPLACE HYGIENE Where goggles are shared between workers, follow the workplace cleaning and disinfection procedure between users. Do not share contaminated eyewear without proper cleaning. Store the goggles away from chemicals, heat and direct sunlight. Keep the strap in good condition and replace it if it no longer holds the frame securely. PRODUCT DETAILS TO CONFIRM This listing identifies one pair of Clear Anti-Fog Safety Goggles. item.title: Steel-Toe Safety Boots
item.description: STEEL-TOE SAFETY BOOTS IN KENYA Steel-Toe Safety Boots are protective work footwear intended for jobs where the feet may be exposed to impact or compression hazards. The listing identifies boots with a steel toe cap and work soles described as slip-resistant. They may be considered for suitable construction, warehouse, workshop, maintenance and industrial tasks. The exact toe-cap rating, sole performance, midsole protection, electrical properties and certification must be confirmed from the supplier before the boots are selected for a regulated workplace. WHY TOE PROTECTION MATTERS A protective toe cap is designed to reduce injury risk if an object falls onto the front of the foot or the toe area is compressed. Safety footwear standards define performance requirements and test methods. For example, EN ISO 20345 specifies safety footwear requirements, including impact and compression protection for certified models. However, the product title alone does not prove that this particular pair has been tested or certified to that standard. Check the markings, manufacturer documentation and declaration of conformity before relying on a rating. CHOOSING THE RIGHT BOOT Select footwear based on the hazards present at the workplace. Consider falling objects, rolling loads, sharp materials, wet floors, oils, chemicals, heat and electrical risks. Not every steel-toe boot provides protection against every hazard. Some models include a puncture-resistant midsole, antistatic properties, fuel- or oil-resistant soles or water-resistant uppers, but those features should not be assumed unless documented for this product. Ask the supplier to confirm the exact specification if the boot is required for a safety-critical role. FIT AND COMFORT Correct sizing is important for both safety and comfort. Choose a size that leaves adequate toe room without allowing the foot to slide excessively. Try the boots with the socks normally worn at work and check that the heel is secure. The boot should allow walking, bending and climbing without pressure points. If workers wear orthotic insoles, confirm that they fit correctly without changing the boot's protective design. For team orders, confirm each worker's size individually. SOLE GRIP AND WORK SURFACES The listing describes a slip-resistant work sole, but actual grip depends on the tread design, floor surface, contaminants and boot condition. A sole suitable for dry concrete may not perform the same on oily, wet or uneven surfaces. Inspect the outsole regularly for worn tread, cracks or separation. Choose footwear specifically rated for the workplace surface and chemical exposure where required. Replace boots when the sole no longer provides reliable traction. CARE AND INSPECTION Inspect the toe area, upper, seams, laces or fasteners, heel and outsole before each work period. Look for cracks, punctures, exposed toe caps, detached soles or damage caused by chemicals and heat. Clean mud and debris using suitable methods and allow the boots to dry naturally. Avoid placing them near direct heat sources that could damage adhesives or materials. Store them in a clean, dry place away from oils, solvents and sharp objects. WORKPLACE PPE PROGRAMME Safety boots are only one part of a workplace PPE programme. Workers may also require gloves, eye protection, hearing protection, hard hats, high-visibility clothing or respiratory protection depending on the job. The employer should carry out a task risk assessment and provide footwear that matches the identified hazards. Do not rely on the phrase steel toe alone as proof of full safety footwear certification. PRODUCT DETAILS TO CONFIRM This listing identifies one pair of Steel-Toe Safety Boots. Confirm the available sizes, toe-cap material, certification standard, sole properties, water resistance, puncture protection and manufacturer markings before ordering. item.title: Disposable CPE Waterproof Shoe Covers – 100 Pack
item.description: DISPOSABLE CPE WATERPROOF SHOE COVERS – 100 PACK IN KENYA Disposable CPE Waterproof Shoe Covers are single-use protective covers designed to fit over ordinary footwear in hygiene-sensitive or controlled areas. This listing identifies a blue 100-piece pack. CPE stands for chlorinated polyethylene, a plastic material used in disposable shoe-cover products. The covers are intended to help keep dirt, dust and moisture from being carried on shoes into clean areas. They are a hygiene barrier, not protective footwear and not a substitute for safety boots where impact, puncture or chemical hazards exist. WHY USE DISPOSABLE SHOE COVERS Shoes can carry dust, soil, moisture and other contaminants from one area to another. A disposable cover provides a temporary outer layer that can help reduce this transfer when workers or visitors enter a controlled space. They may be useful in clinics, laboratories, clean areas, food-processing support zones, cleaning operations, maintenance work and home renovation tasks. The level of protection depends on the cover material, thickness, seams, fit and the conditions in which it is used. Do not assume that every CPE cover is suitable for sterile environments or heavy liquid exposure. MATERIAL AND FIT The product is identified as CPE and the supplier listing describes an elasticated opening designed to help hold the cover around footwear. The elastic edge should sit securely around the shoe without tearing or restricting movement. Choose a cover that fits the footwear size and shape. Oversized covers may drag on the floor or create a trip risk, while undersized covers may split when the wearer walks. Check the pack for the intended size range, material thickness and any textured sole feature before use. WHERE THEY MAY BE USED CPE shoe covers can be useful in medical and laboratory settings, controlled work areas, cleaning operations, food-processing support areas and other environments where reducing shoe-borne dirt is important. They may also be used during maintenance or renovation to help protect indoor floors from mud and dust. The site supervisor should decide whether shoe covers are appropriate for the area and whether a higher level of protective footwear is required. They should not be worn where a loose cover could catch in machinery, stairs or moving equipment. HOW TO PUT THEM ON Put the covers on in a clean area before entering the controlled space. Check that each cover is intact and that the elastic edge is not torn. Pull it over the shoe carefully without stretching the material excessively. Confirm that the cover is fully seated and does not trail under the heel or toe. If the cover splits, slips or becomes heavily contaminated, replace it before continuing. Avoid walking through sharp debris or rough surfaces that can puncture the material. SINGLE-USE HYGIENE AND DISPOSAL The listing describes a single-use product. Do not wash, dry or reuse a disposable cover unless the manufacturer specifically states that reuse is permitted. Remove covers without touching the contaminated outer surface more than necessary. Dispose of used covers in the waste stream required by the facility and the type of contamination. In healthcare or laboratory settings, follow the site's infection-prevention and waste-management procedures. Wash or sanitise hands after removal. LIMITATIONS AND SAFETY Shoe covers are not a replacement for non-slip safety footwear, steel-toe boots, puncture-resistant soles or chemical-resistant boots. A plastic cover can become slippery on wet or polished floors and may tear when exposed to sharp objects. If the task involves chemicals, hot surfaces, heavy objects or moving machinery, select footwear that provides the required protection and do not rely on a disposable shoe cover. Check the risk assessment and supplier instructions. PRODUCT DETAILS TO CONFIRM This listing identifies one 100-piece pack of blue disposable CPE waterproof shoe covers. item.title: Disposable Clear Face Shield
item.description: DISPOSABLE CLEAR FACE SHIELD IN KENYA The Disposable Clear Face Shield is a transparent visor designed to provide a physical barrier in front of the face during suitable splash-prone hygiene, cleaning and workplace tasks. The product record describes a clear full-face visor with an adjustable headband. A face shield can help reduce direct contact of droplets or splashes with the face, but it does not create a sealed barrier around the eyes and should not be used as a substitute for safety goggles, a respirator or other PPE required for the task. WHAT A FACE SHIELD DOES A face shield covers a larger area of the face than ordinary safety glasses. It can provide a barrier in front of the forehead, eyes, nose and mouth against some splashes and droplets, depending on the visor size and fit. It is commonly used as an additional layer alongside other protective equipment. The exact protection depends on the visor material, thickness, side coverage, headband design and the hazard. This listing does not specify a certified impact rating, splash standard or sterility status, so those claims should not be assumed. ADJUSTABLE HEADBAND AND FIT The adjustable headband is intended to help position the visor at a comfortable distance from the face. Adjust it so the shield remains stable when the wearer moves or bends. The visor should cover the face adequately without obstructing normal vision. Check that it does not interfere with prescription glasses, goggles, masks or respirators. If it causes fogging or distortion that prevents safe work, stop and select a suitable alternative. A loose or damaged headband can cause the visor to move unexpectedly. USE WITH OTHER PPE A face shield is usually an additional barrier, not a replacement for eye protection. Where the task creates splashes or flying particles, suitable safety goggles may still be required underneath the shield. If respiratory protection is required, use the respirator specified by the chemical label or workplace risk assessment. The face shield does not filter inhaled air and does not protect the skin on the neck or sides of the face. Do not assume it provides impact protection unless the product is marked and certified for that hazard. SUITABLE WORK SETTINGS Depending on the verified specification, a clear face shield may be used in suitable clinical support, cleaning, maintenance and industrial tasks where a transparent face barrier is appropriate. In a healthcare or laboratory setting, follow the facility's infection-prevention procedure for use, cleaning and disposal. In industrial settings, check whether the visor is rated for impact, heat or chemical splash. The product name alone does not confirm suitability for every application. INSPECTION AND HANDLING Inspect the visor before use for cracks, scratches, clouding, deformation and damaged attachment points. Replace it if visibility is reduced or the headband no longer holds it securely. Avoid placing the clear visor face-down on rough surfaces that may scratch it. Handle the shield by the headband where practical and avoid touching the front surface during contaminated tasks. If the product is disposable, do not reuse it beyond the manufacturer's instructions. CLEANING AND DISPOSAL The current listing describes the item as disposable. Follow the supplier's instructions for cleaning or disposal and do not assume that it can be disinfected repeatedly. If the shield becomes contaminated, remove it using the workplace's safe doffing procedure and dispose of it according to the relevant waste stream. Wash or sanitise hands after removal. Store unused shields in clean packaging away from heat and direct sunlight to prevent warping. PRODUCT DETAILS TO CONFIRM This listing identifies one Disposable Clear Face Shield with a transparent visor and adjustable headband. item.title: Disposable Surgical Gown
item.description: DISPOSABLE SURGICAL GOWN IN KENYA The Disposable Surgical Gown is a single-use protective garment listing for suitable clinical, laboratory and hygiene procedures. A disposable gown can provide an outer barrier between the wearer’s clothing and the work environment, but the actual level of protection depends on its material, construction, seams, cuffs, closure and tested barrier rating. This listing does not specify the gown's sterility, AAMI level, fabric type or fluid-resistance performance. Those details must be confirmed before the gown is selected for a clinical or high-risk procedure. WHY GOWN SPECIFICATION MATTERS Protective gowns are not all interchangeable. Some are intended for basic care or low-risk tasks, while others are designed for procedures with greater exposure to fluids or infectious materials. The FDA recognises the ANSI/AAMI PB70 classification system for liquid-barrier performance of healthcare protective apparel. The levels indicate different barrier performance, from minimal to high. A gown should be chosen based on the anticipated exposure and the manufacturer's verified label, not simply because the product is described as surgical or disposable. CHECK THE LABEL BEFORE USE Before ordering for a healthcare facility, laboratory or clinic, confirm whether the gown is sterile or non-sterile, the intended use, barrier rating if applicable, material, size, sleeve design, cuff type and packaging. A gown intended for routine low-risk care may not be suitable for surgery, invasive procedures or tasks with a significant splash risk. Do not infer that the gown is sterile or certified unless the packaging and supplier documentation explicitly state the relevant standard and status. FIT AND COVERAGE A protective gown should fit the wearer and cover the areas required for the task. Check the garment length, sleeve length, closure method and cuff design. The front and sleeves may need to cover defined body areas depending on the procedure and the applicable gown standard. Ensure the gown can be fastened securely without tearing or leaving unintended gaps. If the garment is too small, too short or poorly closed, it may not provide the expected coverage. PUTTING ON AND REMOVING A DISPOSABLE GOWN Follow the facility's infection-prevention or hygiene procedure for donning and doffing. Perform hand hygiene before putting on the garment and use the required gloves, mask, eye protection and other PPE for the task. Avoid touching the outside of a used gown when removing it. Dispose of the gown in the waste stream specified by the facility and the nature of contamination. A disposable gown should not be washed or reused unless the manufacturer specifically labels it for reuse, which should not be assumed for this listing. SUITABLE SETTINGS Depending on the verified specification, disposable gowns may be used in healthcare, laboratory, cleaning, food-hygiene or other controlled environments where a single-use outer garment is appropriate. The risk assessment should determine whether the garment's barrier performance is adequate. For procedures involving significant fluid exposure, infectious materials or sterile fields, select a gown with the exact performance and sterility status required by the applicable protocol. STORAGE AND DISPOSAL Store unused gowns in their original packaging in a clean, dry area away from direct sunlight, moisture and physical damage. Check the packaging for tears, contamination, expiry or other conditions that could compromise the garment. Keep sizes and stock records so that staff can select the correct fit. Dispose of used gowns according to the facility's infection-control and waste-management procedures. Do not place contaminated garments into ordinary waste if the facility's policy requires a separate stream. PRODUCT DETAILS TO CONFIRM This listing identifies one Disposable Surgical Gown. item.description: INDUSTRIAL POLYCOTTON DUST COAT IN KENYA The Industrial Polycotton Dust Coat is a workwear garment intended to provide a practical outer layer for general duties in workshops, warehouses, cleaning operations and other work environments. It is general workwear, not specialist chemical protective clothing or certified personal protective equipment unless the manufacturer documentation confirms a particular protection standard. WHAT POLYCOTTON WORKWEAR OFFERS Polycotton fabric combines polyester and cotton fibres. The blend is commonly selected for everyday workwear because it can balance comfort, ease of care and durability for routine use. The exact fabric ratio, weight, colour and finish for this coat should be confirmed from the supplier before ordering. A polycotton garment can be useful for staff who need a consistent outer layer during general tasks, but its suitability depends on the workplace conditions and the hazards involved. In a pest-management business, it may be suitable for non-chemical tasks such as equipment handling, stock checks or general site duties. FIT AND SIZE SELECTION Choose a size that allows comfortable movement over the clothing normally worn at work. Check the chest, shoulder, sleeve and coat length measurements against the supplier's size guide. A coat that is too tight can restrict movement, while an excessively loose garment may catch on equipment or door handles. Keep pockets empty during tasks where they may catch on machinery or contaminate materials. Check buttons and seams regularly and repair loose fasteners before the garment is used at work. CARE AND LAUNDERING Follow the garment's care label for washing temperature, detergent, drying and ironing. Remove dust and dirt before washing and inspect the garment for tears, damaged buttons and worn seams. If the coat becomes contaminated with a hazardous chemical, do not launder it as ordinary clothing unless the chemical label and workplace procedure permit that approach. Follow the safety data sheet and employer instructions for contaminated garments and disposal. item.title: Aluminium Brush Door Sweep for Pest Exclusion
item.description: ALUMINIUM BRUSH DOOR SWEEP FOR PEST EXCLUSION IN KENYA The Aluminium Brush Door Sweep for Pest Exclusion is a physical door-sealing accessory designed to reduce the open gap beneath a door. A brush strip fitted along the lower edge can help limit the movement of crawling insects, rodents, dust and outside air through the threshold gap. It is a simple exclusion measure for homes, shops, restaurants, warehouses, offices and other premises where door gaps can create an entry route. It does not replace door repair, structural proofing or a wider pest-management plan. WHY SEAL THE GAP UNDER A DOOR Even a small gap beneath an external door can provide a route for insects, rodents, dust and drafts. A brush door sweep creates a flexible barrier that follows the floor surface as the door opens and closes. It can help reduce access for crawling pests and limit the amount of dust and debris entering the room. The effectiveness depends on the size of the gap, the condition of the threshold, the brush density and the fit along the full door width. It should not be described as a guaranteed rodent-proof barrier. MEASURE BEFORE ORDERING Measure the full width of the door and the clearance between the bottom of the door and the floor. Check whether the floor is level or has a raised threshold, tile joints or uneven sections. The sweep must be wide enough to cover the door width without leaving exposed gaps at either side. The brush length should contact or sit close to the floor without creating excessive friction that prevents the door from closing. Confirm the aluminium rail length, brush height, mounting holes and whether the product can be trimmed before installation. SUITABLE APPLICATIONS Door sweeps may be useful on external doors, service doors, storerooms, utility rooms, kitchens, warehouse access points and other locations where the underside gap needs attention. In a food business, a properly fitted sweep can support pest exclusion by reducing one possible route for crawling pests. It should be combined with door seals, screens, drain covers and other suitable building-proofing measures. For fire doors or doors with specific accessibility requirements, confirm that adding a sweep will not interfere with the door's required operation or compliance. INSTALLATION AND FITTING Clean and dry the lower door surface before fitting. Position the aluminium rail according to the supplier instructions and ensure the brush runs continuously across the opening. Use the correct fixings for the door material and check that screws or other fasteners do not interfere with the door mechanism. If trimming is permitted, cut the rail and brush carefully so that the ends remain neat and no sharp metal edges are exposed. After fitting, open and close the door several times to check that it moves freely and the brush does not drag excessively. MAINTENANCE AND INSPECTION Inspect the brush regularly for bent bristles, trapped dirt, loose screws and gaps at the ends. Clean accumulated dust and debris so that the brush can move freely against the floor. Replace the sweep if the bristles become flattened, damaged or detached. Check the surrounding frame, threshold and wall junctions as well, because pests may use other openings even after the door gap is sealed. A door sweep is most effective when the entire building envelope is maintained. USE WITH AN INTEGRATED PEST-MANAGEMENT PLAN Physical exclusion reduces access, but it does not remove existing pests inside the building. Continue to manage food waste, standing water, clutter and other conditions that support pest activity. Inspect incoming goods and deliveries, keep storage areas tidy and seal other suitable gaps around pipes and service penetrations. If rodents or insects are already established indoors, combine proofing with identification, monitoring and appropriate control measures. item.title: 3M 8210 N95 Disposable Dust Respirator
item.description: 3M 8210 N95 DISPOSABLE DUST RESPIRATOR IN KENYA The 3M 8210 N95 Disposable Dust Respirator is a particulate respirator intended to help reduce exposure to certain airborne non-oil particles when it is correctly selected, fitted and used. It is a cup-shaped respirator with a two-strap design, a nose clip and cushioning nose foam. The model is commonly selected for suitable dusty tasks such as sanding, sweeping and woodworking. It is not a general-purpose gas mask and must not be used for gases, vapours or oxygen-deficient atmospheres. WHAT THE N95 CLASSIFICATION MEANS 3M identifies the 8210 as a NIOSH-approved N95 respirator with at least 95% filtration efficiency against certain non-oil-based particles under the applicable test conditions. This rating relates to particulate filtration; it does not mean the respirator blocks every airborne hazard or provides protection in every work environment. The product does not protect against gases, vapours, oil aerosols or low-oxygen conditions. For pesticide handling, chemical spraying or fumigation, select respiratory protection from the chemical label, safety data sheet and workplace risk assessment. A particulate respirator alone may be unsuitable for those tasks. DESIGN AND FIT The 8210 has a cup-shaped facepiece, welded dual-point strap attachments, a metal nose clip and soft nose foam. The two straps are designed to help hold the respirator in position and support a close face seal. A respirator only works as intended when it fits the individual wearer. Facial hair, incorrect strap placement, damage or poor adjustment can create leakage around the edges. Users should follow the official 3M fitting instructions and the applicable workplace respiratory-protection programme. PUTTING ON AND CHECKING THE RESPIRATOR Inspect the respirator before use for holes, tears, damaged straps, a bent nose clip or other defects. Place it over the nose and mouth with the lower edge under the chin, position the upper strap high on the back of the head and the lower strap below the ears around the neck. Shape the nose clip using both hands so it follows the bridge of the nose. Perform the user seal check described in the 3M instructions each time the respirator is donned. If air leaks around the face, readjust it; if a proper seal cannot be achieved, do not continue using that respirator for the task. WORK TASKS AND LIMITATIONS The 3M 8210 may be considered for suitable non-oil particulate exposures such as dust generated by sanding, sweeping or woodworking, subject to the hazard assessment and local requirements. It should not be selected solely because a task looks dusty. Some dusts are toxic, fibrogenic or otherwise require a formal respiratory-protection programme and a different respirator or supplied-air system. Do not use it in environments where oxygen is insufficient or where gases and vapours are present. Never assume it is appropriate for insecticide vapours, solvent vapours or thermal fogging. FIT TESTING, TRAINING AND REPLACEMENT Workplaces that require respirators should follow the relevant occupational-safety requirements, including medical evaluation, fit testing where required, training and a documented respiratory-protection programme. A user seal check is not a substitute for formal fit testing. Replace the respirator if it becomes damaged, contaminated, difficult to breathe through or unable to maintain a seal. The 8210 is a disposable respirator; do not wash it or attempt to disinfect it for reuse unless the manufacturer specifically authorises a method for the exact product. STORAGE AND HANDLING Keep unused respirators in their original packaging in a clean, dry place away from direct sunlight, chemicals, moisture and crushing. Check the manufacturer's shelf-life information and packaging condition before use. Store away from dust and contaminants so that the respirator remains clean before it is worn. item.title: UV Insect Killer Replacement Tubes – Pair
item.description: UV INSECT KILLER REPLACEMENT TUBES – PAIR IN KENYA UV Insect Killer Replacement Tubes – Pair is a two-tube replacement listing for compatible electric insect light traps. Insect light traps use ultraviolet-A lamps to attract flying insects towards a capture mechanism such as an adhesive board or an internal grid. Over time, fluorescent tubes can lose output or stop working, so replacement may be needed to keep a compatible unit operating as intended. This listing is for a pair of tubes, not a complete insect killer. CHECK COMPATIBILITY BEFORE ORDERING UV tubes are not universal. Different insect light traps can use different wattages, lengths, tube diameters, pin bases, electrical arrangements and lamp types. Before ordering, switch off and isolate the existing unit, then check the label or manual for the exact replacement part specification. Compare the tube length, wattage, base configuration and model number. Do not select a tube only because it looks similar. A wrong tube may not fit, may not operate correctly or may damage the equipment. UNDERSTAND THE ROLE OF THE UV TUBE The lamp provides the light source that attracts certain flying insects. The insect trap's capture method depends on the unit design. Some units use glue boards to retain insects; others use an electrified grid. The station is not rodent bait itself, and purchasing the housing does not by itself eliminate rodents. WHY USE AN ENCLOSED BAIT STATION Loose bait can be disturbed, contaminated or reached by people and non-target animals. A suitable tamper-resistant station helps restrict casual access when it is correctly locked, secured and positioned. It can also protect bait from some dust, debris and environmental exposure. For pest-management professionals, fixed bait points make it easier to map activity, inspect consumption and maintain a consistent service record. The station should always be treated as one part of a broader integrated programme that includes sanitation, proofing and monitoring. SUITABLE LOCATIONS AND PLANNING Potential locations may include building perimeters, service corridors, utility areas, waste-management zones and other places where rodent signs have been identified. The exact placement depends on the site, rodent behaviour, station design and the label directions for the bait selected. A trained operator should assess likely runways, entry points, harbourage and food sources before installing stations. Do not place bait stations in food-preparation areas or where bait could contaminate food, utensils or packaging. Avoid positions where routine cleaning, deliveries or vehicle movement could damage or dislodge the unit. USING THE STATION RESPONSIBLY Use only bait or compatible monitoring inserts that are suitable for this specific station. Confirm the station's internal dimensions and bait-retention method before ordering replacement bait. Follow the rodenticide label for approved use, handling, inspection and disposal. Do not cut, break or repackage bait unless the product instructions expressly permit it. Keep bait and the station secured away from children, pets, livestock and wildlife. Where a site requires a documented pest-control programme, label and map each station in line with the operator's procedures and applicable requirements. INSPECTION AND SERVICE RECORDS A station should not be installed and then forgotten. Check it at intervals appropriate to the site risk and product label. During inspection, confirm that the housing remains closed and secured, the station has not moved, and the bait or monitoring insert has not been damaged or contaminated. Record the station reference, location, inspection date, observations and any service action. If there is evidence of tampering, damage, non-target access or bait spillage, secure the area and follow the product safety instructions. Never handle rodenticide bait with bare hands. INTEGRATED RODENT MANAGEMENT Bait stations work best alongside practical measures that reduce the conditions attracting rodents. Keep refuse in closed containers, remove food spills, store food and animal feed in rodent-resistant containers, and correct leaking water sources. Seal suitable gaps around pipes, doors and service penetrations with materials appropriate to the structure. Manage vegetation and clutter around buildings where these create hiding places. Monitor droppings, gnaw marks, tracks and other signs to understand whether activity is changing. If activity continues, reassess the site rather than relying on bait alone. item.title: Pantry Moth Pheromone Sticky Trap
item.description: PANTRY MOTH PHEROMONE STICKY TRAP IN KENYA The Pantry Moth Pheromone Sticky Trap is a monitoring tool for kitchens, food cupboards, dry-goods stores and other places where packaged or stored food is kept. Pantry moths can become noticeable when small moths fly around cupboards, larvae appear near dry foods, or fine webbing is found inside food packaging. A pheromone trap helps you check whether adult moth activity is present and whether it changes after you have cleaned and inspected the storage area. It is a monitoring aid, not a complete treatment for an established infestation. HOW THE PHEROMONE TRAP WORKS The lure is intended to attract adult moths of the target pantry-moth group to the sticky adhesive surface. When an attracted moth lands on the board, it becomes caught and can be counted during routine inspection. This gives a visible indication of activity and can help a household, shop, restaurant or food-store operator decide whether a closer inspection is needed. The trap does not spray insecticide onto food and should not be treated as a substitute for removing infested food or cleaning storage shelves. WHERE TO USE IT Consider monitoring dry-food storage areas where flour, cereals, rice, maize meal, nuts, dried fruit, seeds, pet food or similar products are stored. In a home, suitable monitoring points may include a pantry cupboard, a dry-food cabinet or a shelf near previously affected packages. In a shop or commercial store, place monitoring devices in suitable non-food-contact positions around dry-goods storage zones. Do not place the adhesive surface where it can touch unpackaged food, food-contact equipment or preparation surfaces. INSPECTION AND PREVENTION Before setting a trap, inspect stored foods and packaging for signs of infestation. Check seams, folds, corners and the underside of shelves. Discard food that is clearly infested in a sealed bag and clean the affected storage area thoroughly. Vacuum cracks and shelf joints where crumbs or residues may collect, then dispose of the vacuum contents safely. Store susceptible dry foods in clean, tightly closed containers and avoid keeping old, opened packets for long periods. These housekeeping steps address sources that a monitoring trap cannot remove. POSITIONING AND MAINTENANCE Follow the supplier's instructions for assembling, activating and positioning the trap. Keep it dry and away from direct contact with food, water, dust and excessive heat. Place it where it can be checked easily but cannot be handled by children or pets. Record the date it is installed and inspect it at regular intervals. Replace the trap when the adhesive becomes dusty, full or no longer effective, and follow the pack guidance for lure life and disposal. Do not assume a trap remains active indefinitely. WHO MAY FIND IT USEFUL The trap may be useful for households, mini-markets, supermarkets, restaurants, bakeries, hotels, food handlers and managers responsible for dry-goods storage. It can also support a professional pest-management inspection by helping identify where adult moth activity is being detected. In a business, use a simple monitoring log to note trap location, inspection date and catch observations. A rising catch or repeated activity should prompt inspection of nearby stock and storage practices rather than simply adding more traps. IMPORTANT PRODUCT INFORMATION This listing is for a pheromone-based sticky monitoring trap. The exact lure composition, target species, dimensions, replacement interval and number of traps supplied should be confirmed from the product pack or supplier before use. Do not infer that the product controls larvae inside food or eliminates every life stage. Keep the trap away from children, pets and non-target insects, and dispose of used adhesive material responsibly. item.description: CLOTHES MOTH PHEROMONE TRAP FOR WARDROBES AND STORAGE IN KENYA The Moths Pheromone Trap for Wardrobes and Storage is a sticky monitoring device for checking adult moth activity around clothing, wardrobes, closets, linen cupboards and textile-storage areas. Clothes moth activity can be difficult to notice at first because damage may occur in quiet, undisturbed parts of a wardrobe or storage room. A pheromone trap can help reveal the presence of adult moths and indicate whether an inspection of nearby fabrics and stored items is needed. It is a monitoring aid; it does not repair damaged clothing or remove larvae hidden in fabrics. HOW A PHEROMONE MONITORING TRAP HELPS The lure is intended to attract adult moths from the target group to an adhesive surface. Captured moths provide a visible record that can be checked over time. This information may help a household, hotel, laundry, uniform store, clothing retailer or textile manager identify where moth activity is being detected. A trap should not be interpreted as proof that every garment is infested, nor does an empty trap prove that no moths or larvae are present. Monitoring results need to be considered alongside a careful inspection. WHERE TO POSITION IT Potential monitoring points include wardrobes, closets, linen stores, carpet-storage areas and shelves holding natural-fibre textiles. Place the trap where it can be inspected easily but will not touch clothing, bedding or other fabrics. Keep it away from children, pets, direct contact with water and areas where it may be crushed or covered. Follow the supplier's instructions for placement distance, activation and replacement. The exact target species and lure coverage should be confirmed from the pack. INSPECT FABRICS AND STORAGE AREAS When moth activity is suspected, inspect stored garments, blankets, carpets, upholstery and other susceptible textiles. Pay attention to seams, folds, collars, cuffs, pockets, hems and dark undisturbed corners. Look for irregular holes, larvae, shed skins, cases or fine debris. Check stored items before moving them to another room because infested textiles can spread the problem. Empty the affected storage area and vacuum shelf joints, skirting edges and cracks. Dispose of vacuum contents in a sealed bag. CLEANING AND PREVENTION Clean garments according to their care labels. Where suitable, laundering, professional cleaning or other approved fabric-care methods may help address eggs or larvae. Do not apply pesticides to clothing or bedding unless the product label specifically permits that use. Store clean seasonal clothing in clean, sealed containers or garment bags. Reduce dust and lint accumulation, and avoid storing worn clothing for long periods without cleaning. Inspect second-hand textiles and items returning from storage before placing them in wardrobes. MONITORING IN HOMES AND BUSINESSES For a home, a simple record can include the trap location, installation date and observations at each check. In hotels, guest houses, laundries, clothing shops and uniform stores, assign each trap a reference so that results can be compared across rooms or storage zones. A repeated catch in one area should trigger a closer inspection and review of storage and cleaning routines. If damage continues or multiple areas show activity, a professional inspection can help distinguish clothes moths from other fabric pests and recommend an appropriate response. PRODUCT DETAILS AND CARE This listing describes a pheromone sticky trap for wardrobe and textile-storage monitoring. Confirm the number of traps supplied, dimensions, lure type, target moth species and recommended replacement interval from the supplier's packaging. item.description: RODIRID RODENTICIDE WAX BLOCKS IN KENYA RodiRid Rodenticide Wax Blocks are rodent-control bait blocks intended for use in a properly planned rat-management programme. The block format is designed for controlled placement in suitable baiting points, normally using a compatible, secured bait station where required by the product label and site conditions. Rodenticides are hazardous products and must never be treated like ordinary household items. Read the exact pack label before use and ensure the product is suitable for the intended site and target pest. UNDERSTAND THE PRODUCT BEFORE USE The name identifies this listing as RodiRid wax-block rodenticide, but customers should confirm the exact formulation, active ingredient concentration, block weight, pack quantity, registration details and directions printed on the current pack. Product formulations and pack sizes can differ. Do not rely on a generic online description for dosage, baiting intervals or safety instructions. The label supplied with the product is the controlling source for approved uses, precautions, first aid and disposal. If the pack is damaged, unlabelled or does not match the item ordered, do not use it. WHY WAX BLOCKS ARE USED Wax-block baits are designed to provide a formed bait unit that can be placed in suitable baiting equipment. Depending on the product formulation, the block format may be selected for locations where a firm bait unit is easier to secure and inspect than loose grain bait. A bait block can support a monitoring record because an operator can check whether the bait point has been disturbed or consumed. This does not mean the bait is waterproof in every situation or suitable for every environment; check the manufacturer's instructions and inspect the station regularly. SAFE BAITING PRINCIPLES Rodenticide bait should be handled only by a responsible person who understands the label. Use appropriate protective equipment specified on the pack, avoid skin contact and wash hands after handling. Never place bait where children, pets, livestock, birds or other non-target animals can reach it. Do not place it on food-contact surfaces, in food-preparation areas or near food and animal feed. Secure bait inside a compatible station when required, and ensure stations cannot be easily moved or opened by unauthorised people. Do not transfer bait into unmarked containers. SITE ASSESSMENT AND MONITORING Before a baiting programme begins, inspect the premises for droppings, gnaw marks, runways, burrows, damaged packaging and other evidence of rodent activity. Identify likely access routes and food or water sources. A professional operator can use this information to plan suitable bait points and decide whether baiting is appropriate. During follow-up inspections, record each point, check the condition of the station and note bait take or other activity. Remove spilled bait promptly using the method stated on the label. Dispose of used packaging and any contaminated material as directed. REDUCE THE CONDITIONS THAT ATTRACT RODENTS Baiting should be combined with good housekeeping and proofing. Keep refuse covered, clean food spills quickly, store dry goods in sealed containers and avoid leaving animal feed exposed overnight. Repair gaps around doors, pipes and service entries using suitable materials. Reduce clutter and vegetation close to buildings where these provide harbourage. These measures reduce access to food and shelter and help prevent reinvasion after control work. STORAGE, FIRST AID AND DISPOSAL Keep the product in its original labelled packaging, locked away from children and animals, and separate from food, drink and animal feed. Follow the label for temperature, moisture and storage requirements. If accidental exposure or suspected poisoning occurs, seek urgent medical or veterinary advice as appropriate and take the product label or packaging with you. INSPECTION AND MAINTENANCE During a service visit, check that the cover is correctly fitted and that the station is not cracked, distorted or loose. Look for signs of tampering, water ingress, debris or damage. If the cover no longer closes properly or does not match the station body, do not rely on it to secure bait. Follow the station manufacturer's instructions for cleaning and replacement. Record the station location and service date where the unit is part of a commercial pest-management programme. Do not use a damaged accessory in a way that compromises station security. RODENT PREVENTION BEYOND BAIT STATIONS A well-managed bait station is only one part of rodent prevention. Keep waste in covered bins, clean food residues, store dry goods and animal feed in sealed containers, repair leaking taps and remove clutter that can provide shelter.
